note: The GM-side read of a document, and what every document write answers with. A FIELD is a top-level key of data - one flat, snake_case namespace per type (CANVAS-19). Which keys a type has, and what kind of value each holds, is a registry fact (registry.json): common fields for every type, plus the type's own. All eight types declare their fields (1kg.5.3); a key a type does not name fails closed. Nothing here says who may see a field: the per-field rule in registry.json does, following ED-5, and the mask that acts on it is agent-forge-harness-1kg.1.6's.

invalid.name: field keys named like JavaScript built-ins
invalid.why: not declared, like any other stray key. The client half of this case is in contracts.test.ts: such a key must read as 'not declared' there too, never resolve to something on a prototype

invalid.name: an ability block with an ability the rules do not have, which a client strips
invalid.why: 1kg.5.3: the ability block has a closed key set, and a response is read the tolerant way — the client drops what it does not know so a type can gain structure without a version bump. The server still refuses to emit it

invalid.name: a field the type does not declare
invalid.why: X-8 and the bead's AC: invalid document fields fail closed. The server never stores or emits a key outside the type's definition

invalid.name: the handoff's camelCase key
invalid.why: snake_case everywhere on the wire, nested document data included: ifAttacked is if_attacked

data.name: Sister Ondrey Vashe
data.ifAttacked: She walks into the water and is gone.

invalid.name: another type's field
invalid.why: fields are declared per type: wants belongs to an NPC, not to session notes

invalid.name: a portrait that carries a URL
invalid.why: X-10: an asset is named by id and a client builds a same-origin URL; a document can never point a browser at a remote host

invalid.name: a document without a name
invalid.why: LIB-12: every document has a name from the moment it exists; it is its title everywhere

invalid.name: an empty name
invalid.why: a name is 1 to 200 characters; it is the one field that cannot be cleared

invalid.name: a text field of 201 characters
invalid.why: a text field is one line of at most 200 characters

invalid.name: a lone surrogate in a text field
invalid.why: JSON allows the escape; UTF-8 does not, so no stored field can hold one and neither validator accepts one

invalid.name: a line break in a text field
invalid.why: a text field is one line; paragraphs belong in a prose field

invalid.name: a prose field of 20,001 characters
invalid.why: RAIL-6: field caps are checked before any provider work, so a pasted book is not re-sent on every edit

invalid.name: a number where prose belongs
invalid.why: no coercion

invalid.name: tags as one comma-separated string
invalid.why: a list field is a list

invalid.name: an empty item in a list
invalid.why: a list item is 1 to 2,000 characters; removing an item removes it

invalid.name: 101 tags
invalid.why: a list holds at most 100 items

invalid.name: a cleared text field written as null
invalid.why: one way to say empty per kind: text and prose clear to the empty string, both lists to [], and an asset, an integer and an ability block to null

invalid.name: a document type that does not exist
invalid.why: X-8: a closed set; never rendered as an NPC by default, which is what the handoff's registry fallback did

invalid.name: a type version this contract does not know
invalid.why: field definitions are versioned per type (1kg.5.3); the strict schema knows version 1, and parseDocument turns a newer one into a placeholder

invalid.name: a write revision of zero
invalid.why: CANVAS-34: the write revision counts committed writes, and creating a document is the first

invalid.name: the handoff's version id used as the concurrency token
invalid.why: CANVAS-34: history and concurrency are different things; a write revision is an integer counter, never a version label

invalid.name: the handoff's reveal mask riding on the document
invalid.why: reveal is server state with its own resource (REVEAL-5, CANVAS-33), and what may be shown to whom waits for 1ir.1.2; a document body carries neither

invalid.name: the whole history riding on the document
invalid.why: CANVAS-27: history is its own page, 20 at a time; a document carries its current version only

invalid.name: no campaign
invalid.why: a document belongs to exactly one campaign; a client drops a response for another (LIB-25)

invalid.name: a handout whose illustration is an audio asset
invalid.why: an asset field on a document is an image; audio is a cue and never a document field

invalid.name: a quest log whose threads are bare strings
invalid.why: 1kg.5.3: an entry_list holds {name, text} entries, not a text_list - the renderer shows the name as a heading

invalid.name: a character sheet whose armour class is text
invalid.why: 1kg.5.3: ac is an integer field, so no renderer ever has to parse it

invalid.name: a lore entry carrying an npc's field
invalid.why: X-8 and the type's definition: a key another type declares is still undeclared here, and fails closed

invalid.name: an encounter whose party level is a decimal
invalid.why: an integer field takes a whole number, and 3.5 is not one on either side

invalid.name: an integer field one past the top of its range
invalid.why: 1,000,001 is one past the ceiling. A drift in either language's constant would make this example pass on one side only

invalid.name: an integer field one past the bottom of its range
invalid.why: -1,000,001 is one past the floor; the range is symmetric and both ends are checked

invalid.name: an ability score one past its ceiling
invalid.why: an ability score stops at 99. A client that reads a higher one and a server that stores it are the drift this example exists to catch

invalid.name: an ability score below its floor
invalid.why: 0 is the floor - a creature that lacks an ability has none of it, and a modifier is never stored here

invalid.name: an entry list of 101 entries
invalid.why: an entry_list holds at most 100 entries

invalid.name: an entry name of 201 characters
invalid.why: an entry's name is a text field: one line of at most 200 characters, because a renderer shows it as a heading

invalid.name: an entry text of 2,001 characters
invalid.why: RAIL-6: an entry's text is a list item, capped at 2,000 characters so a pasted page is refused before any provider work

invalid.name: a line break in an entry name
invalid.why: an entry's name is one line, like every other text field; the body of the entry is where paragraphs go
